draft.title: Scams and identity theft
card: a trick that gets people to hand over money or personal details. Scammers often pretend to be a bank, a business or a government agency.
using another person's stolen details, such as their name, birth date or bank details, to commit fraud. The thief may open accounts or take out loans in the victim's name.
A scam can lead to identity theft. If a person shares their details with a fake bank, the scammer can then use those details as their own.
Warning signs include a message that creates pressure to act fast, asks for passwords or card details, or comes from a sender the person did not expect.
draft.remember: A scam is the trick. Identity theft is using stolen details to commit fraud.

a.q: Which situation is an example of identity theft?
opts: A thief uses Sam's stolen details to take out a loan
A shop raises the price of a game Sam wanted to buy
A bank sends Sam a letter about a change in its fees
Sam loses money when a shared investment falls in value
a.why: Identity theft is using someone else's details to commit fraud, and taking out a loan in Sam's name does this. A price rise or a fall in value is a normal market change, not fraud.
a.clue: Look for the option where someone else uses Sam's details.

b.q: Priya gets a text that looks like it is from her bank. It says her account is locked and she must click a link and enter her password within one hour. What is the best description of this message?
opts: A scam that tries to get her personal details
Identity theft that has already happened to her
A normal security step that banks use to protect accounts
A loyalty offer sent to customers who save regularly
b.why: The message pretends to be a bank and pressures Priya to share her password, so it is a scam. It is not yet identity theft, because nothing has been used to commit fraud. That could only happen if she shares her details.
b.clue: Has anyone used her details yet, or is this still a trick to get them?

a.best: A thief uses Sam's stolen details to take out a loan

b.best: A scam that tries to get her personal details

problems.detail: Why (b) says identity theft 'could only happen if she shares her details'. The card says a scam 'can' lead to identity theft. Identity theft can also happen in other ways, such as data breaches or stolen mail, so 'only' overstates the card and is not true.

The right option is the only one using the words 'thief' and 'stolen details', which echo 'identity theft' in the question. The distractors involve no wrongdoing at all, so a student can pick the answer from the word match without understanding the idea.

check.summary: Both answers are clear and correct. Why (b) wrongly says identity theft could 'only' happen if Priya shares her details, and the right option in question a gives itself away by echoing 'theft' with 'thief' and 'stolen details'.

a.q: Which situation is an example of identity theft?
opts: Someone uses Sam's details to open a phone account
A caller posing as Sam's bank asks for his card number
A fake online shop takes Sam's money and sends nothing
A text says Sam won a prize but must pay a fee first
a.why: Identity theft is using another person's details to commit fraud, and opening an account in Sam's name does this. The caller asking for his card number is a scam: it tries to get his details, but they have not been used yet. The fake shop and the prize text are scams that trick him into paying.
